note_5_label_access_truncation.detail: verify() still returns True for a tail-truncated log whose head_hash is refit to the new last entry -- inherent to a self-describing hash chain with no external length/head commitment. This was a v1 NOTE, not a failing row: verify() detects edits, reorders, substitutions, and sealed-role injection ('tamper of any entry'), just not omission of a trailing read in isolation. The implementer deferred it to manifest-anchoring follow-up (commit head_hash + entry count into the lineage/evidence manifest so completeness is externally checkable). ACCEPTABLE for this gate: no sealed gold becomes reachable, no committed read can be silently altered, and the anchor is a Plan-3-adjacent provenance task rather than a Plan-2 contract defect.

note_N10_raw_deletion_temporal_ordering.detail: The delete-coverage check verifies each extract-derived raw location is a member covered by SOME delete_raw target, but not that the covering deletion occurs AFTER that particular extract. So a plan that re-extracts a raw path after its delete_raw (or after launch) is accepted, leaving an orphaned raw directory present at launch (concrete input N10 / Q2). This does NOT violate the row-4 security requirement: the launched inputs remain strictly sanctioned (materialize_input destinations under /inputs, outside all raw locations), so no launched input reaches the surviving raw (Q1 rejected). It also creates no new raw-text-to-model path beyond the pre-existing, accepted content-trust boundary of materialize_input (whose SOURCE is unmodeled in both v1 and v2 designs; an executor is trusted to copy only sanctioned content). RECOMMENDED HARDENING (not blocking): require the covering delete_raw to occur at a step index greater than the last extract of that path, and/or forbid extract steps after launch. Flagged for the implementer as follow-up alongside note 5.

challenge_summary: Re-ran both v1 escapes (B5 case-variant, B6 nested) -> now rejected by the structural guard. Ran nine new escapes against the reworked guard: launch input not materialized, materialize target outside /inputs, '..' traversal, undeleted extract, decoy delete target, trailing-slash normalization, launch input inside the raw tree, empty launch inputs, and a case-variant raw input -> all correctly handled (N6 trailing-slash correctly accepted as legitimate). Directly probed the security property (Q1): a launch input pointing at surviving raw is rejected. Found one temporal-ordering robustness gap (N10/Q2): an orphaned raw directory can survive into launch via a late re-extract, but no launched input can reach it -- recorded as a non-blocking hardening recommendation. Verified forecast conservatism floors (safety_buffer>=0.20, reserve_usd>0) reject the v1 'false go' and the go=>affordable invariant holds over 20,000 randomized inputs. Spot-checked corrections 1,2,3,5,6 for regression (none; most are byte-unchanged by the fix).
